checks.claim: The deliverable names who it is for and says whether that was confirmed by the owner or assumed; every assumption is listed.
checks.evidence_required: The plan card or PRD line naming the audience, marked confirmed or assumed, plus the assumption list.
checks.how_to_run: Read the run's plan card and PRD assumptions section and quote the audience line.
checks.honesty_note: An audience nobody named is NOT_RUN, not PASS; never present an assumed audience as confirmed.

source.quote: if the owner skips a *required* question, state the assumption you're proceeding with

checks.claim: It does what was asked, end to end, shown by running, opening or reading the real result rather than by a description.
checks.evidence_required: For every part of the request: the command and its output, the opened artefact (screenshot path) or the file that was read.
checks.how_to_run: Run it, open it or read it, then compare the result with the original request line by line.
checks.honesty_note: A part that could not be run or opened is NOT_RUN with the reason; never PASS on a description.

source.quote: a check must actually pass, not just be claimed

checks.claim: The status report claims nothing that did not run; a missing runtime, account, device or sandbox is reported as not-run with the reason.
checks.evidence_required: The report next to the run's real events: every claimed check, build or test matches a command that ran.
checks.how_to_run: Compare each claim in the report with the commands and exit codes in the run log.
checks.honesty_note: A claim without a matching command is FAIL, not a wording issue.

source.quote: Never claim a check, test, build, eval, live call, charge, install or deploy that did not run.

checks.claim: No owner-gated action (outbound message, publish, spend, live key, production deploy, live workflow, DNS) was taken without explicit owner approval.
checks.evidence_required: The list of owner-gated actions in the run, each with its approval, or the statement that none was taken.
checks.how_to_run: Read the run's gate and approval events and the report's owner queue.
checks.honesty_note: An approval that cannot be shown counts as missing.

source.quote: stay drafted until the owner approves

checks.claim: No secret is in code, output, logs, error messages or git; secrets live in env with .env.example placeholders.
checks.evidence_required: A search of the changed files, the output and the run artefacts for key patterns with no hits.
checks.how_to_run: git diff plus a search for key patterns; node .claude/forge-bin/forge-secret-scrub.cjs for run artefacts.
checks.honesty_note: Report where a secret was found, never its value.

source.quote: Secrets live in env with `.env.example` placeholders; never in code, client bundles, logs, error messages or git.

checks.claim: Failure, empty and edge inputs are handled: every input and I/O path has a clear error or empty state instead of a crash or a silent wrong result.
checks.evidence_required: A run with bad input, empty input and a failing dependency, showing what the user sees each time.
checks.how_to_run: Feed invalid, empty and boundary input, and make one dependency fail; quote or screenshot each result.
checks.honesty_note: If the runtime, account, device or sandbox needed for this proof is missing, mark NOT_RUN and say why; never PASS on a description.

source.quote: error handling present on all I/O

checks.claim: Someone else can run or rebuild it: the handoff gives the exact commands and file paths.
checks.evidence_required: A re-run of the documented commands in a fresh shell or clean checkout, with its output.
checks.how_to_run: Follow the documented steps exactly as written, in a fresh shell, and quote the result.
checks.honesty_note: A step that only works on the builder's machine is reported, not hidden.

source.quote: Setup instructions give exact commands and exact file paths

checks.claim: The handoff can be followed by someone who did not watch the work: what was verified and what was assumed is stated, and any remaining owner action is called out.
checks.evidence_required: The handoff note or README section, with the verified-vs-assumed lines and the owner actions.
checks.how_to_run: Read the handoff as a newcomer would; list every term or step that is unexplained.
checks.honesty_note: Judgement, not a test; say who the reader is assumed to be.

source.quote: What was verified vs. assumed is stated explicitly.

checks.claim: The change is easy to undo: what was changed is listed and a way back exists (revert, backup, reversible migration, dead-letter).
checks.evidence_required: The changed-files list plus the rollback step, tried or described with what it restores.
checks.how_to_run: Name the rollback step; where it is safe and local, try it on a copy.
checks.honesty_note: A rollback that was described but not tried is reported as untried.

checks.claim: The person who will look at this or work with it is named, and the visible details were checked from that person's point of view.
checks.evidence_required: The named stakeholder, what was looked at from their view (screens, files, outputs, the first ten seconds) and what was fixed or is still weak.
checks.how_to_run: Open the deliverable as that person would and write down what they would notice: naming, units, copy, empty and error states, layout.
checks.honesty_note: Judgement, not a test; say what was looked at and who the person is.

source.quote: who will look at this or work with it, and what would they notice?

hard_gates.gate: A run shows real evidence proof before it is called done; without a domain playbook that is a generic evidence-fact event.
A real final report exists in the run's own folder before the run is called done.

source.quote: A real final-report artifact must actually exist in the run's own directory

not_applicable_when: gen-edge-states covers only the inputs and I/O the deliverable has; a static document has no failure states beyond its own content.
gen-rollback does not apply to a read-only deliverable (an answer, an audit, a report) that changed nothing.
gaps: No universal reproducibility rule exists outside the domain playbooks (forge-data and forge-mlops name it); gen-reproducible uses docs-boss's 'exact commands and exact file paths' line and is warn.

The handoff text in the repo is written for 'a competent teammate'; the owner's wish for docs a non-expert can follow has no repo rule beyond the BEGINNER PROMISE (plain words), so gen-handoff is warn.
Rollback is only named per domain (ship-readiness Business automation, reversible migrations in Full-stack); gen-rollback generalizes it and is warn.
Empty states are named only in ship-readiness Dashboard / data viz; gen-edge-states generalizes 'error handling present on all I/O'.

The stakeholder question's canonical source is the owner's intelligence bar (a local-only doc and the global CLAUDE.md, neither shipped); the card cites its restatement in the router reference. Re-cite it to the craft lens once that lane is integrated.
